items.title: 聯合干預難敵賣壓 憂日元匯率再逼近160關卡 日企要求5-10年「超長天期」避險
items.title_en: Joint Interventions Struggle Against Selling Pressure, Yen Nears 160 Threshold, Japanese Firms Seek 5‑10‑Year “Ultra‑Long‑Term” Hedging
paras: 日元匯率近期再度逼近1美元兌160日元關卡，儘管美日政府曾在2022年、2024年及2026年進行聯合匯市干預，但日元走勢依然疲軟。
日元持續走弱大幅拉高了日本進口商的成本。連鎖超市Takara MC執行長Taku Ueno表示，從美國引進牛肉及從歐洲進口橄欖油等商品的成本日益高昂。Ueno指出，因匯率變動劇烈，美牛價格談判已從每月一次改為每三個月一次，以求延緩終端零售價格上漲。
他認為，「日本正失去購買力」，採購時常面臨中國與泰國買家的競爭，甚至必須親自拜訪供應商求購。此外，日本家具大廠Nitori Holdings估算，日元兌美元每貶值1元，其利潤將縮減約20億日元。
日本經濟新聞編輯委員小栗太指出，雖然官方干預對象主要是避險基金等投機資金，但在日本供需環境改變下，基於實際需求賣出日元的力道正逐步增強。
面對這波匯率波動，日本企業紛紛透過遠期外匯、期貨與選擇權等金融工具進行避險。大和證券執行董事Akira Hirayama透露，過去企業避險多為數月至一年，現已有客戶尋求鎖定長達5至10年的匯率。
推動日元長期貶值的主要因素之一，在於日本相對低利的環境及日本央行緩慢的升息步伐。對於未來走勢，市場仍顯保守。摩根大通日本銷售主管Daiki Hayashi分析，包含境外帳戶在內的多數投資人仍持懷疑態度，主流意見認為日元匯率將維持在155至165區間。
美國銀行外匯銷售主管Namato Nagahama表示，雖然出口商開始考慮避險鎖利，但日元此前一再跌破市場預期的關鍵價位，目前尚難斷定匯率是否已見頂。
paras_en: The yen has again approached the 160 per dollar level, and despite joint market interventions by the U.S. and Japanese governments in 2022, 2024 and 2026, the currency remains weak.

The yen’s continued weakness has sharply raised costs for Japanese importers. Takara MC CEO Taku Ueno said that the cost of importing U.S. beef and European olive oil is soaring. He noted that because of volatile exchange rates, negotiations for U.S. beef have shifted from monthly to once every three months to try to delay retail price hikes.

He believes “Japan is losing purchasing power,” and that procurement often faces competition from Chinese and Thai buyers, sometimes requiring personal visits to suppliers. In addition, furniture giant Nitori Holdings estimates that a one‑yen depreciation against the dollar would cut its profit by about ¥2 billion.

Nikkei editor‑in‑chief Oguri Tai pointed out that while official interventions mainly target hedge funds and other speculative capital, the force of selling yen for genuine demand is gradually strengthening as Japan’s supply‑demand dynamics change.

Facing the currency swing, Japanese companies are hedging with forwards, futures and options. Daiwa Securities executive director Akira Hirayama said that while hedges used to be for a few months to a year, clients are now seeking to lock in rates for as long as five to ten years.

One of the main drivers of the yen’s long‑term decline is Japan’s relatively low‑interest environment and the Bank of Japan’s slow rate‑hiking pace. Looking ahead, markets remain cautious. JPMorgan Japan sales head Daiki Hayashi noted that most investors, including those with offshore accounts, remain skeptical, with the consensus view that the yen will stay in a 155‑165 range.

Bank of America FX sales head Namato Nagahama said that although exporters are beginning to consider hedging to lock in profits, the yen has repeatedly broken key market‑expectation levels, making it still unclear whether the currency has topped out.

items.title: 〈台幣〉升貶互見收在31.818元 升值5分
items.title_en: New Taiwan Dollar shows mixed movement, closes at 31.818, up 0.05
paras: 新台幣今(26)日持續呈現升貶互見，終場收在31.818元，升值5分，台北外匯經紀公司成交值12.02億美元，維持量縮盤整格局。
新台幣今日以31.83元、升值3.8分開出後，最高來到31.809元，最低則見到31.877元，早盤多空拉鋸，午盤過後則主要為升值，高低價差7.8分。
觀察主要亞幣，日元升值近0.2%，新台幣收升0.16%，人民幣和星元處平盤左右，韓元貶值近0.1%，泰銖貶約0.15%，而美元指數小彈0.05%左右。
統一投顧表示，伊朗和阿曼討論臨時框架，市場對荷姆茲海峽能源運輸恢復有期待，因此油價重挫且美債殖利率回落，接著聯準會主席華許周五將在全球央行年會發表談話，投資人密切留意其是否維持既有立場，以及對通膨、利率與聯準會溝通政策的最新說法。
也有法人提到，美國最新公布的8月諮商會消費者信心指數與7月新屋銷售數據，均不如市場預期，令10年期公債殖利率下行，也舒緩市場對通膨和高利率的擔憂。
paras_en: The New Taiwan dollar continued to show mixed movement today (26th), closing at 31.818, up 5 points. Taipei foreign exchange brokerage firm recorded a turnover of US$1.202 billion, maintaining a low-volume consolidation pattern.

The New Taiwan dollar opened at 31.83, up 3.8 points, then rose to a high of 31.809 and fell to a low of 31.877. The early session saw a tug‑of‑war between buyers and sellers; after the midday session the bias was mainly upward, with a high‑low range of 7.8 points.

Among major Asian currencies, the Japanese yen appreciated about 0.2%, the New Taiwan dollar rose 0.16%, the Chinese yuan and Singapore dollar were roughly flat, the South Korean won depreciated about 0.1%, the Thai baht fell about 0.15%, while the US dollar index slipped roughly 0.05%.

Unified Investment Advisory noted that Iran and Oman are discussing a temporary framework, and the market is hopeful for the resumption of energy shipments through the Hormuz Strait. Consequently, oil prices have dropped sharply and U.S. Treasury yields have retreated. Moreover, Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell will deliver a speech at the Global Central Bank Meeting on Friday; investors are closely watching whether he will maintain the current stance and his latest comments on inflation, interest rates, and the Fed’s communication policy.

Some institutional investors also pointed out that the latest U.S. August Consumer Confidence Index released by the Conference Board and July new‑home sales data both fell short of expectations, pushing 10‑year Treasury yields lower and easing market concerns about inflation and high interest rates.

items.title: 澳洲退休基金巨頭逆勢看多日元 大舉押注市場低估日銀升息前景
items.title_en: Australian Pension Giant Takes Contrarian Bullish Stance on Yen, Bets Heavily Market Underestimates BOJ Rate Hike Prospects
paras: 澳洲第二大退休基金澳洲退休信託(Australian Retirement Trust)(ART)近期逆勢建立多年來最大的日元超配部位，押注市場低估了日本央行(BOJ)的升息前景。
這家管理約 3700 億澳元(約 2650 億美元)退休儲蓄的巨頭，在過去6個月中，隨著日元兌美元跌向 160，持續增加日元曝險，而部分資金來自削減美元的配置。
ART 高級投資組合經理 Jimmy Louca 指出，雖然市場已充分計價能源價格上漲對日元的拖累，但對日本央行升息的預期依然不足。他認為，若這兩個因素逆轉，將為極具價格吸引力的日元提供支撐。
目前互換市場預期日本央行 9 月升息概率約 80%，最遲於 10 月將行動完全定價。Louca 預期，央行可能在下月升息，並可能釋放再升息兩次的信號，這有望推動日本公債殖利率進一步走高，而他預估美元兌日元的公允價值約為 150，甚至可能跌至 140 至 149 的區間。
除了外匯市場，ART 對日本的布局也延伸至股市，於 2026 年 3 月增加了日本股票持倉，並特別聚焦於能直接受益於利率上升的金融板塊。相反地，ART 對美債採取減配約 0.5 個百分點的立場。
Louca 認為，高於目標的通膨、具韌性的增長和 AI 投資熱潮將推高美債殖利率；他並警告，雖然美元仍因儲備貨幣地位而具備重要的避險功能，但試圖壓低名目殖利率的舉措，可能會引發通膨並削弱美元。
paras_en: Australia's second-largest pension fund, Australian Retirement Trust (ART), has recently taken a contrarian stance to build its largest yen overweight position in years, betting that the market is underestimating the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) rate hike prospects.

The giant, which manages approximately AUD 370 billion (about USD 265 billion) in retirement savings, has steadily increased its yen exposure over the past six months as the yen weakened toward 160 against the US dollar, funding part of the move by trimming its US dollar allocation.

ART senior portfolio manager Jimmy Louca noted that while the market has fully priced in the drag on the yen from rising energy prices, expectations for BOJ rate hikes remain insufficient. He believes that a reversal in these two factors would provide support for the yen, which he considers highly attractively valued.

Swap markets currently price in an approximately 80% probability of a BOJ rate hike in September, with action fully priced in by October at the latest. Louca expects the central bank to hike rates next month and potentially signal two further increases, which could push Japanese government bond yields higher. He estimates the fair value of the USD/JPY pair at around 150, with the potential to fall into the 140 to 149 range.

Beyond the foreign exchange market, ART's Japan exposure has also extended to equities, with the fund increasing its Japanese stock holdings in March 2026, particularly focusing on the financial sector, which stands to benefit directly from rising interest rates. Conversely, ART has adopted a stance of underweighting US Treasuries by approximately 0.5 percentage points.

Louca believes that above-target inflation, resilient growth, and the AI investment boom will push US Treasury yields higher. He also warned that while the US dollar retains its important safe-haven status due to its reserve currency role, attempts to suppress nominal yields could spark inflation and weaken the dollar.

items.title: 【遠東商銀】德國數據較佳，提供歐元支撐
items.title_en: Far East Commercial Bank: Better German Data Provides Euro Support
paras: ◆USD/JPY

美國擴大對伊朗次級制裁範圍，警告各國切斷與伊朗的商業聯繫，否則關鍵企業和實體面臨排出美元金融體系之外風險，藉此切斷支撐伊朗的每一條經濟生命線，伊朗則誓言報復美國擴大經濟制裁，但消費者新聞與商業頻道(CNBC)報導，美國財政部可能動用部分現金餘額回購長期公債，以緩解融資成本壓力，週二導致美元乏力，而且日本財務大臣片山皋月稱，政府將仔細研究提供日本公債散戶投資者稅收優惠，或能填補日本央行(BOJ)減持公債的缺口，成為維持市場穩定關鍵，提供日圓支撐，美元兌日圓下滑至158.99低點。

隨著日本公債收益率大幅上升，今年迄今日本債券交易所交易基金(ETF)吸引創紀錄15億美元淨流入，但BOJ下修7月核心消費者物價指數(CPI)至較上年同期升2.2%，並據共同社報導，日本財務省預計各部門及機構2027財政年預算申請總額首次超過130兆日圓達創紀錄36.64兆日圓，償債成本將升17%，恐加劇財政壓力，引發日圓走貶；此外，美國7月新房屋價格中位數較去年同期創四年新低0.9%及銷售量減10.5%至年率60.7萬戶為1月以來最低，而且美國8月消費者信心指數跌至七個月低點89.4，但波士頓聯邦儲備銀行總裁柯林斯稱若通貨膨脹無持續回落，需盡快加息，而且美國聯邦準備理事會(FED)上月貼現率會議紀錄顯示十二個地區中四家FED董事會支持上調貼現率25個基點，推升美元兌日圓至159.48高點。預估今日美元兌日圓支撐於158.80-159.00，阻力於159.60-80。
◆EUR/USD
昨日澳洲央行(RBA)的8月會議紀錄顯示，九名政策委員對是否加息意見不一，數名認為通貨膨脹存在上行風險，可能有必要加息，但距離加息決定比市場先前預期更近，12月升息的概率升至68%，而且紐西蘭央行(RBNZ)料下周上調25個基點的機率為90%及年底利率進一步升至3.0%，令澳幣和紐元保持堅挺，帶動歐元兌美元穩守1.1650低點。

items.title: 貶值壓力難解 日央行9月升息機率飆至57% 多數經濟學家押注利率升至1.25%
items.title_en: Depreciation Pressure Remains Unresolved, BOJ's September Rate Hike Odds Surge to 57% as Most Economists Bet on 1.25% Rate
paras: 日本銀行(BOJ)升息步伐可能明顯加快。路透最新調查顯示，多數經濟學家預期，日本央行最快將在9月再度升息，將目前1%的政策利率調升至1.25%，市場對最終利率的預期也同步上修。推動政策轉向的因素包括中東戰事推升進口能源成本、日元持續承壓，以及日本國內通膨壓力升高，使日本央行面臨更強烈的提前收緊貨幣政策壓力。
路透於8月17日至24日進行的調查顯示，57%的受訪經濟學家預期日本央行將在9月升息，與7月調查時僅5%的受訪者預期本季採取行動相比出現明顯逆轉。58名回答利率時點問題的受訪者中，有10人預期日本央行將在10月或12月進一步升息，將政策利率提高至1.5%。
日本央行6月已將政策利率調升至1%，創約30年來新高。市場目前關注焦點已從日本央行是否繼續升息，轉向升息速度以及本輪緊縮週期的最終利率水準。
摩根大通證券首席日本經濟學家藤田綾子(Ayako Fujita)表示，市場已在很大程度上消化日本央行9月升息的預期，如果央行此時延後行動，反而可能造成市場不穩定，因此提早調整政策已變得難以避免。
市場對日本央行中長期緊縮幅度的預期也顯著提高。54名受訪分析師中，有35人、約三分之二預期，到2027年3月底前政策利率至少將升至1.5%，比7月調查預期的時間提前約3個月。另有約60%的受訪者預期，到2027年第3季底前，日本政策利率至少將達到1.75%。
對最終利率的預期同樣大幅上修。在回答額外問題的36名受訪者中，50%認為1.75%將成為本輪緊縮週期的最終利率，高於7月時的19%；預期最終利率將達2%或更高的比例，也從7月的23%升至36%，顯示市場對日本央行政策正常化的預期正快速升溫。
日本央行近期政策討論也顯示，決策官員對加快升息步伐的支持正在擴大。部分官員認為，隨著通膨持續高於央行2%的目標，日本央行需要進一步撤回貨幣寬鬆措施；也有官員主張避免承諾固定升息節奏，但應向市場展現防止物價持續偏離目標的決心。
最新通膨數據進一步強化升息理由。日本7月核心消費者物價指數(CPI)年增1.8%，高於6月的1.6%，主要受到進口成本及能源價格變化影響。排除生鮮食品與能源後的核心通膨率也由1.7%升至1.9%，服務業通膨則持續受到薪資成長支撐，顯示日本物價壓力並未完全消退。
中東局勢成為日本貨幣政策的新變數。美國與以色列對伊朗的軍事行動及後續衝突推升油價，對高度依賴能源進口的日本形成更直接的通膨壓力。日本央行擔心，如果能源與進口成本持續攀升，加上日元維持疲弱，可能進一步推高物價預期，迫使央行加快收緊政策。
日元持續走弱也是日本央行面臨的另一項壓力。日本與美國上月罕見聯手干預匯市，在日元跌至40年低點附近後進場買進日元，以遏制日元與日本公債同步遭拋售所可能引發的外溢風險。
不過，最新調查顯示，市場對單靠匯市干預扭轉日元弱勢並不樂觀。在26名回答相關問題的經濟學家中，有18人、超過三分之二認為干預效果「不太有效」或「完全無效」，不少人認為相關行動只是延後問題爆發，並未解決日元貶值的根本因素。
美國財政部長貝森特(Scott Bessent)近期的發言也進一步強化9月升息預期。路透先前報導，日本央行正考慮最快9月升息，並評估在之後以比目前約每年兩次更快的速度推進緊縮政策。貝森特對日元與日本貨幣政策的關注，也被市場視為增加日本央行提前行動壓力的因素之一。
另一方面，日本首相高市早苗的財政政策可能與日本央行的抗通膨努力形成拉鋸。調查中28名回答相關問題的經濟學家裡，有25人、占89%認為，高市政府的財政政策將加劇日元走弱。
市場擔心，如果政府推動食品減稅與擴大投資支出，卻無法提出明確財源，可能進一步加重日本財政疑慮，導致日元與日本公債面臨新的拋售壓力。
野村證券首席經濟學家森田京平(Kyohei Morita)指出，高市政府的財政政策可能推高通膨預期，也加深市場對日本央行在控制物價上落後於情勢的疑慮。他警告，如果在市場已擔心缺乏財源支持的情況下進一步削減消費稅，海外投資人拋售日本公債可能加速日元貶值。
日本企業近期也開始為長期日元弱勢做準備。日元過去數年大幅貶值，導致進口能源、原物料及其他商品成本增加，企業正增加使用遠期、期貨與選擇權等工具避險。市場普遍認為，如果日本央行未能有效縮小與海外主要市場的利差或穩定通膨，日元仍可能長期維持弱勢。
日本公債市場也增加日本央行決策的複雜性。隨著殖利率上升，日本國債重新吸引部分海外資金，但更高的利率同時增加日本政府融資成本。日本央行若9月升息，可能有助於穩定日元，卻也可能進一步推升政府與企業融資成本，考驗日本龐大債務負擔及債市穩定。
整體而言，最新調查顯示，市場對日本央行政策路徑的預期已從「是否繼續升息」，轉向「升息速度會有多快、最終利率會有多高」。在日元弱勢、進口通膨、中東能源衝擊與財政擴張疑慮交織下，日本央行9月會議可能成為決定新一輪政策緊縮節奏的重要轉折點。若央行如市場預期升息至1.25%，將是日本利率正常化進程的進一步加速，也可能為2027年前後利率升向1.5%甚至1.75%以上鋪路。
paras_en: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) may accelerate its rate‑hike pace markedly. Reuters' latest survey shows most economists expect the BOJ to raise rates again as early as September, lifting the current 1% policy rate to 1.25%, and market expectations for the final rate have been revised upward accordingly. Drivers of a policy shift include higher imported energy costs from the Middle‑East conflict, continued yen weakness, and rising domestic inflation pressure, all putting stronger pre‑emptive tightening pressure on the BOJ.

Reuters’ survey conducted from Aug. 17‑24 found 57% of respondents expect a September hike, a sharp reversal from July when only 5% anticipated action this quarter. Of the 58 economists who answered the timing question, 10 foresee a further hike in Oct. or Dec., taking the policy rate to 1.5%.

The BOJ lifted its policy rate to 1% in June, a near‑30‑year high. Market focus has shifted from whether the BOJ will keep raising rates to how fast it will do so and what the final level of this tightening cycle will be.

Ayako Fujita, chief Japan economist at JPMorgan Securities, said the market has largely priced in a September hike; a delay now could destabilise markets, making an early policy adjustment hard to avoid.

Long‑term tightening expectations have also risen sharply. Among 54 surveyed analysts, 35 – about two‑thirds – expect the policy rate to be at least 1.5% by the end of March 2027, roughly three months earlier than July’s forecast. Around 60% anticipate the rate will reach at least 1.75% by the end of Q3 2027.

Final‑rate expectations have been revised upward as well. Of 36 respondents to a follow‑up question, 50% now see 1.75% as the ultimate rate for this cycle, up from 19% in July; the share expecting a final rate of 2% or higher rose from 23% to 36%, indicating a rapid warming of market expectations for BOJ normalisation.

Recent BOJ policy discussions show growing support among decision‑makers for a faster hike pace. Some officials argue that with inflation persistently above the 2% target, the BOJ must further unwind monetary easing; others caution against committing to a fixed hike rhythm but say the bank should demonstrate resolve to keep prices on target.

The latest inflation data further bolster the case for hikes. Japan’s core CPI rose 1.8% year‑on‑year in July, up from 1.6% in June, driven mainly by import costs and energy price changes. Core‑core inflation (excluding fresh food and energy) climbed from 1.7% to 1.9%, and services inflation remains supported by wage growth, showing price pressure has not fully abated.

Middle‑East tensions have become a new variable for Japanese monetary policy. U.S. and Israeli military actions against Iran and ensuing conflict have pushed oil prices higher, creating a more direct inflationary shock for Japan, which relies heavily on energy imports. The BOJ worries that sustained rises in energy and import costs, combined with a weak yen, could lift inflation expectations and force a faster tightening.

A persistently weak yen is another pressure on the BOJ. Japan and the United States jointly intervened in the FX market last month after the yen slipped toward a 40‑year low, buying yen to curb simultaneous selling of the yen and Japanese government bonds and avert spill‑over risks.

However, the latest survey shows scepticism about the effectiveness of FX intervention alone. Among 26 economists who answered the related question, 18 – more than two‑thirds – consider intervention “not very effective” or “completely ineffective,” with many saying such actions merely postpone the problem rather than address the root cause of yen depreciation.

Recent comments by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have further reinforced September‑hike expectations. Reuters previously reported that the BOJ is weighing a September hike and may accelerate tightening to a pace faster than the current roughly twice‑a‑year cadence. Bessent’s focus on the yen and Japanese policy is seen as adding pressure for the BOJ to act early.

On the fiscal side, Prime Minister Kishida’s policies could clash with the BOJ’s anti‑inflation effort. Of the 28 economists surveyed on this issue, 25 (89%) believe the Kishida administration’s fiscal stance will exacerbate yen weakness.

Markets fear that if the government pushes food tax cuts and expands investment spending without clear financing, fiscal concerns could deepen, prompting fresh selling pressure on the yen and Japanese government bonds.

Nomura chief economist Kyohei Morita warned that Kishida’s fiscal plan could raise inflation expectations and deepen doubts about the BOJ’s ability to control prices. He cautioned that further consumption‑tax cuts amid concerns over funding could trigger overseas investors to dump Japanese bonds, accelerating yen depreciation.

Japanese firms are already preparing for a prolonged yen weakness. The yen’s sharp depreciation over recent years has raised import costs for energy, raw materials and other goods, prompting companies to increase hedging with forwards, futures and options. The market broadly believes that if the BOJ cannot narrow the yield gap with overseas markets or tame inflation, the yen may stay weak for the long term.

The Japanese bond market adds another layer of complexity to BOJ decisions. Rising yields have begun to attract some foreign capital back to JGBs, but higher rates also raise the government’s financing costs. A September hike could help stabilise the yen but would also push up borrowing costs for the government and corporations, testing Japan’s massive debt load and bond‑market stability.

Overall, the latest survey shows market expectations have shifted from “whether the BOJ will keep raising rates” to “how fast the hikes will come and how high the final rate will be.” Amid yen weakness, import‑driven inflation, Middle‑East energy shocks and fiscal‑expansion worries, the September BOJ meeting could become a pivotal turning point for the next tightening cycle. If the BOJ lifts rates to 1.25% as markets expect, it would further accelerate Japan’s rate‑normalisation path and could pave the way for rates of 1.5% or even 1.75%+ by around 2027.

paras: 美元周二(26日)走弱，市場風險情緒受到油價與美國公債殖利率下滑的帶動而升溫。同時，加拿大幣在前一個交易日走跌後小幅反彈，加拿大政府以報復性關稅反制華盛頓的措施。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數(DXY)下跌0.1%，報98.93。目前徘徊在5月中旬以來最低水準附近。
固定收益市場持續受到外匯市場參與者的關注，美國公債殖利率連續第二個交易日走低。一項關鍵推動因素是CNBC周一的一則報導，稱華盛頓可能動用規模近1兆美元的財政部一般帳戶(TGA)，協助為上周宣布增加的長天期公債回購提供資金。市場將這項措施視為一項出乎意料的干預行動，目的是抑制殖利率上升，尤其是長天期殖利率。
經濟學家與分析師普遍認為，美國財政部的干預只是針對更大問題所採取的不可持續短期解決方案，而這個更大的問題受到華盛頓財政債務不斷膨脹所引發的市場擔憂所推動。上周，美國政府債務突破40兆美元，導致財政部宣布措施後所帶來的全部漲幅遭到逆轉。
一般而言，公債殖利率上升會產生類似升息的效果，因為這會推高消費者與企業的借貸成本，通常有利於美元走強。然而，上周美國債務的消息引發了市場對美國財政狀況的疑慮，而在這種環境下，投資人傾向將資金從法定貨幣轉向黃金或加密貨幣等硬資產。
事實上，美元指數上周下跌近1%，黃金與加密貨幣均上漲。
Macquarie全球外匯與利率策略師Thierry Wizman表示，「美元昨天收復了上周跌幅的一小部分，但我們認為，市場更重要的變化，是美國長天期公債殖利率自上周中旬觸及高點後持續下降。」
他表示，「也許有些交易員注意到了自昨天開始出現的報導(或外洩消息)，稱美國財政部長貝森特(Scott Bessent)可能會動用財政部一般帳戶，以擴大長天期公債的回購規模。視干預規模而定，這將是另一項試圖管理長天期公債淨供給的措施，這些債券會發行至高評級長天期債券市場。」
Wizman補充，「任何旨在單純透過降低市場流通中的美國政府債務平均剩餘期限來『扭轉』美國殖利率曲線的操作，本身並不一定代表貨幣政策具『刺激性』，也不會單獨創造刺激性的財政效果。它也沒有直接處理赤字『問題』。但債務管理政策仍可能非常有用，具體取決於干預的規模，而非其對殖利率的影響。」
目前利率市場目前關注焦點已轉向周三公布的7月核心個人消費支出(PCE)物價指數數據，該指標被廣泛視為聯準會(Fed)偏好的通膨衡量指標。之後市場焦點將轉向聯準會主席華許(Kevin Warsh)周五在傑克森霍爾(Jackson Hole)年度會議上的主題演講。
加拿大出手反擊 加幣反彈
其他主要貨幣方面，加拿大幣兌美元走強，美元兌加幣下跌0.1%，至1.3827加幣。
加幣前一個交易日走弱，因華盛頓與渥太華為達成貿易協議所進行的談判破裂，而新的50%美國關稅於周六開始生效，適用於價值276億美元的加拿大進口商品。
加拿大周二表示，自9月8日起，將「對美國根據第338條款與第232條款關稅所針對的產品徵收15%、25%及50%的報復性關稅，各項產品的稅率將與美國相應的稅率一致。」
根據加拿大政府的聲明，這些關稅將適用於價值276億美元的美國進口商品，涵蓋鋼鐵、乳製品、家電、農業設備、紙漿與紙張，以及電子產品等產業。
英鎊兌美元上漲0.1%，至1.3650美元，受到英國公債殖利率保持韌性及服務業價格走勢強勁的支撐。
歐元兌美元小幅上漲0.1%，至1.1674美元，在區域交易員消化德國經濟成長優於預期的數據後，延續近期漲勢。德國國內生產毛額(GDP)年增率達1.0%，高於市場預期。
日元兌美元持平，美元兌日元匯率維持在159.10不變。

paras_en: The dollar weakened on Tuesday (the 26th) as risk sentiment was lifted by falling oil prices and a drop in U.S. Treasury yields. At the same time, the Canadian dollar, after falling the previous trading day, made a modest rebound as Canada imposed retaliatory tariffs in response to Washington's measures.
In the New York close, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the greenback against six major currencies, fell 0.1% to 98.93, hovering near its lowest level since mid‑May.

The fixed‑income market continues to draw attention from forex participants, with U.S. Treasury yields slipping for the second consecutive session. A key driver was a CNBC report on Monday that Washington might tap the Treasury’s General Account (TGA), roughly $1 trillion, to fund the expanded long‑term Treasury repurchase announced last week. Markets saw this as an unexpected intervention aimed at curbing rising yields, especially at the long end.

Economists and analysts generally view the Treasury’s move as an unsustainable short‑term fix to a larger problem driven by concerns over Washington’s ever‑growing fiscal debt. Last week U.S. government debt topped $40 trillion, causing the gains from the Treasury’s announcement to be quickly erased.

Normally, higher bond yields act like a rate hike, raising borrowing costs for consumers and firms and typically supporting a stronger dollar. However, last week’s debt news sparked doubts about U.S. fiscal health, prompting investors to shift money from fiat currencies into hard assets such as gold and cryptocurrencies.
In fact, the dollar index fell nearly 1% last week, while gold and crypto both rose.

Macquarie global FX and rates strategist Thierry Wizman said, “The dollar reclaimed a small portion of last week’s losses yesterday, but the more important market shift is the continued decline in long‑term U.S. Treasury yields since they peaked in mid‑week.”

He added, “Some traders may have noticed reports (or leaks) starting yesterday that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent could draw on the General Account to expand the scale of long‑term Treasury repurchases. Depending on the size of the intervention, this would be another attempt to manage the net supply of long‑dated bonds issued to the high‑grade market.”

Wizman further noted, “Any operation that simply tries to ‘flatten’ the U.S. yield curve by shortening the average remaining maturity of debt in circulation does not necessarily represent a ‘stimulative’ monetary policy, nor does it create a standalone fiscal stimulus. It also does not directly address the deficit ‘problem.’ However, debt‑management policy can still be very useful, depending on the scale of the intervention rather than its immediate impact on yields.”

The focus in the rates market has now shifted to the July core personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index due on Wednesday, a metric widely regarded as the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge. After that, attention will turn to Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh’s keynote speech at the annual Jackson Hole conference on Friday.
Canada strikes back – the loonie rebounds
Among other major currencies, the Canadian dollar strengthened against the U.S. dollar, with USD/CAD down 0.1% to 1.3827 CAD.

The loonie had weakened the previous session after negotiations between Washington and Ottawa over a trade deal collapsed, and a new 50% U.S. tariff took effect on Saturday covering $27.6 billion of Canadian imports.

Canada said on Tuesday that, starting September 8, it will impose retaliatory tariffs of 15%, 25% and 50% on U.S. products subject to tariffs under sections 338 and 232, matching the corresponding U.S. rates for each product category.

According to the Canadian statement, the tariffs will apply to $27.6 billion of U.S. imports, covering steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics, among other sectors.
The British pound rose 0.1% against the dollar to $1.3650, supported by resilient UK gilt yields and strong services‑price trends.
The euro edged up 0.1% to $1.1674 as regional traders digested Germany’s better‑than‑expected growth data, extending the recent rally. German GDP grew 1.0% year‑on‑year, above forecasts.
The yen was flat against the dollar, with USD/JPY unchanged at 159.10.
The Australian dollar gained 0.2% to $0.7164. Minutes from the RBA’s August meeting showed policymakers remain divided on whether persistently high core inflation justifies another rate hike.

items.title: 美國要把中國銀行踢出美元圈？北京早已留好一條後路
items.title_en: U.S. Plans to Expel Chinese Banks from the Dollar System? Beijing Has Already Prepared a Back‑Up Plan
paras: 美國威脅將協助伊朗規避制裁的企業及金融機構逐出美元體系，使中國大型銀行陷入兩難。北京雖公開反對美國單邊制裁，但中國的貿易及金融活動仍高度依賴美元，主要銀行也有強烈誘因維持與美國金融體系的連結。
美國財政部長貝森特(Scott Bessent)本周一宣布，任何替伊朗洗錢或規避制裁的實體，都可能被切斷與美國金融體系的聯繫。這項措施是美國總統川普對伊朗發動「經濟版D-Day」的一部分。
貝森特被問及中國銀行是否可能成為制裁目標時表示，若相關銀行協助進行交易，參與將伊朗石油轉換成資金、再用於鎮壓活動的金融生態系，美國就會採取行動。
中國外交部周二(25日)回應，北京一貫反對未獲國際法依據或聯合國安理會授權的非法單邊制裁，並將採取「一切必要措施」維護自身權益。
中國高度依賴伊朗石油。美中經濟暨安全檢討委員會分析師3月指出，在美伊戰爭爆發前，中國買下伊朗約九成出口原油，相當於中國原油進口總量約12%，也是伊朗最大貿易夥伴。

人民幣支付系統成地緣避險工具

美國擴大實施「經濟放逐行動」(Operation Economic Outcast)，點名多家中國企業及個人涉嫌協助伊朗軍方，並表示將給予各國一定期限停止相關活動，但未公開具體日期。
儘管北京態度強硬，分析人士認為，中國仍會設法留在美元融資體系，同時加速建立降低制裁風險的替代管道。Z-Ben駐上海董事總經理Peter Alexander指出，人民幣跨境支付系統(CIPS)顯示中國正尋求分散對美元金融體系的依賴，但並非完全放棄美元。
中國人民銀行2012年開始建設CIPS，恰逢美國財政部因涉及伊朗非法交易制裁中國規模較小的崑崙銀行。俄烏戰爭2022年爆發後，CIPS交易量明顯增加，今年整體也持續成長。
目前CIPS在全球共有210家直接參與機構，多數是中國國有銀行的海外分支機構。中國也藉由雙邊貨幣互換擴大人民幣使用，阿根廷及澳洲本月均與中國續簽貨幣互換協議，使雙方央行可交換價值數百億美元的人民幣。
Alexander表示，新興金融體系不代表各國將拋棄美元，而是提供一種「地緣政治避險工具」。
美元目前仍占全球支付主導地位。根據國際銀行金融電信協會(SWIFT)資料，美元7月占全球支付比重逾五成，人民幣則以3.1%排名第五，低於2025年初的逾4%。在貿易融資方面，美元占比接近八成，人民幣以8.4%排名第二。

制裁與稀土籌碼牽制美中雙方

經濟學人智庫(EIU)資深經濟學家Tianchen Xu表示，中國希望留在有利其出口引擎運作的美元體系內，但不代表北京會全面配合美國不斷擴大的制裁。若華府對中國大型企業下手，中國可能利用稀土出口管制及其他措施反擊。
美國同樣需要中國掌握的關鍵礦產，因此也有維持雙邊關係穩定的誘因。川普5月訪問北京後，預計下月底在美國再次與中國國家主席習近平會面。Eurasia Group中國區主任Dan Wang認為，華府不希望伊朗問題破壞這場峰會。
她指出，美中關係的核心仍是台灣問題，中伊關係並沒有外界想像中緊密，北京自2018年以來基本上已停止對伊朗提供國家支持的基礎建設投資。
不過，若美國將中國大型銀行逐出SWIFT，將大幅增加人民幣貶值壓力，這是北京難以接受的結果。自2月28日美伊戰爭爆發以來，美元指數上漲約1.5%，人民幣兌美元則升值近2%，兌歐元升值逾3%。
中國今年曾協助美伊在巴基斯坦展開初步和平談判，但分析人士認為，北京既缺乏能力，也沒有意願迫使任何一方談判。Alexander表示，中國甚至還沒開始真正對美國採取強硬手段；問題並非華府可以做什麼，而是美國最終是否真的敢執行制裁。
paras_en: The United States threatens to expel companies and financial institutions that help Iran evade sanctions from the dollar system, putting Chinese major banks in a dilemma. Beijing publicly opposes unilateral sanctions, yet China’s trade and financial activities remain heavily dependent on the dollar, and its main banks have strong incentives to maintain ties with the U.S. financial system.

U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced on Monday that any entity assisting in money‑laundering or sanction evasion for Iran could be cut off from the U.S. financial system. This measure is part of President Trump’s “economic D‑Day” against Iran.
When asked whether Chinese banks could become targets, Bessent said that if a bank helps facilitate transactions that convert Iranian oil into funds used to suppress activities, the U.S. would act.

On Tuesday (the 25th), China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs responded, reiterating its opposition to unilateral sanctions lacking international law or UN Security Council authorization, and vowed to take “all necessary measures” to protect its interests.

China relies heavily on Iranian oil. An analyst from the U.S.–China Economic and Security Review Commission noted in March that before the U.S.–Iran war, China bought about 90% of Iran’s exported crude, accounting for roughly 12% of China’s total oil imports and making Iran its largest trading partner.

The renminbi payment system becomes a geopolitical hedge tool. The U.S. expands its “Economic Outcast” operation, naming several Chinese companies and individuals suspected of aiding the Iranian military, and says it will give countries a certain period to halt related activities, though no specific dates are disclosed.

Despite Beijing’s hard stance, analysts believe China will still find ways to stay in the dollar financing system while accelerating the creation of alternative channels that reduce sanction risk. Peter Alexander, Z‑Ben’s Managing Director in Shanghai, noted that the Cross‑Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) shows China seeking to diversify its dependence on the U.S. financial system, but not to abandon the dollar entirely.

The People’s Bank of China began building CIPS in 2012, coinciding with the U.S. Treasury sanctioning the smaller Kunlun Bank for illicit Iranian transactions. After the 2022 Russia‑Ukraine war, CIPS transaction volume increased noticeably and has continued to grow this year.

Currently, CIPS has 210 direct participants worldwide, most of which are overseas branches of Chinese state banks. China also expands renminbi use through bilateral currency swaps; Argentina and Australia renewed currency swap agreements with China this month, allowing their central banks to exchange hundreds of billions of dollars in renminbi.
Alexander said that emerging financial systems do not mean countries will abandon the dollar, but rather provide a “geopolitical hedge tool.”

The dollar still dominates global payments. According to SWIFT data, the dollar accounted for over 50% of global payments in July, while the renminbi ranked fifth at 3.1%, below the over 4% it had at the start of 2025. In trade finance, the dollar’s share is nearly 80%, with the renminbi at 8.4% ranking second.

Sanctions and rare‑earth leverage restrain both sides. Tianchen Xu, a senior economist at the Economist Intelligence Unit, said China wants to stay in the dollar system that benefits its export engine, but that Beijing will not fully comply with the U.S.’s expanding sanctions. If Washington targets large Chinese firms, China could retaliate with rare‑earth export controls and other measures.

The U.S. also needs key minerals that China controls, creating incentives to keep bilateral relations stable. After Trump’s May visit to Beijing, a second meeting with President Xi is expected at the end of the month. Dan Wang, Director of Eurasia Group’s China office, believes Washington does not want the Iran issue to derail the summit.

He noted that the core of U.S.–China relations remains the Taiwan issue, and that China‑Iran relations are not as close as outsiders imagine. Since 2018, China has largely stopped providing state‑backed infrastructure investment to Iran.

However, if the U.S. removes Chinese major banks from SWIFT, it would sharply increase pressure on the renminbi to depreciate, a result Beijing cannot accept. Since the U.S.–Iran war began on February 28, the dollar index has risen about 1.5%, the renminbi has appreciated nearly 2% against the dollar, and against the euro it has risen over 3%.

China helped the U.S. and Iran launch preliminary peace talks in Pakistan this year, but analysts say Beijing lacks both the capacity and willingness to force either side to negotiate. Alexander noted that China has not yet truly taken hard measures against the U.S.; the issue is not what Washington can do, but whether the U.S. ultimately dares to enforce sanctions.
